name: Grenadine
label: Simple Machines
lede: Two label bosses and a trombonist put down the guitars and the noise and made a crooning, cocktail-hour pop record about Goya products.

eras.title: Three scenes, one lounge act
eras.text: Mark Robinson of Unrest, Jenny Toomey of Tsunami and Rob Christiansen of Eggs were each running or living inside the DC-area indie world. Grenadine was the side project where none of them had to sound like their day bands.

years.h: Robinson, Toomey and Christiansen form Grenadine
years.p: Wikipedia dates the start to 1991. Robinson and Toomey sing and play guitar; Christiansen plays trombone, guitar and drums.
years.xp: Robinson ran Teenbeat and fronted Unrest, Toomey co-ran Simple Machines and sang in Tsunami, and Christiansen played in Eggs. The trio's sound was described as indie-lounge-pop, a crooning cocktail act that drew comparisons to Rudy Vallee.

years.h: Triology single on Teenbeat and Simple Machines
years.p: The debut single came out on Robinson's and Toomey's labels together, a split-the-bill arrangement the band kept for its whole run.

eras.title: Goya
eras.text: Kramer produced the first album, and the trio built a whole aesthetic around Goya foods. It was the record where the three voices fit best.

years.h: Goya: Kramer produces a joint release from three labels
years.p: The album came out on Simple Machines, Teenbeat and Kramer's Shimmy Disc, with song titles like "Philco" and "Decca" that look back to old radios and records.
years.xp: Trouser Press praised the airiness and clarity Kramer brought and singled out a cover of a Flamingos song, sung with Art Garfunkel-style vocals. It judged the debut the more successful blend of the three players. Wikipedia dates the album to 1992; Trouser Press lists 1993.

years.h: "Don't Forget the Halo" single on Teenbeat and Simple Machines
years.p: The second single arrived between the two albums, again as a joint release from Robinson's and Toomey's labels.

eras.title: Nopalitos and Christiansen
eras.text: The second round came with a new producer and a rougher mood, plus a solo EP for the trombonist.

years.h: Nopalitos: Warren Defever takes over the board
years.p: The second album was produced by Warren Defever of His Name Is Alive and released on Simple Machines and Teenbeat.
years.xp: Trouser Press heard more conflict this time, with Robinson's whimsical excursions set against Toomey's darker seriousness, and a cavalier take on an older song. Its verdict: the second shot of Grenadine was one too many. The trio's own Simple Machines page describes them as a band that hardly ever played live.

years.h: Christiansen EP puts the trombonist up front
years.p: Rob Christiansen got his own EP on Teenbeat and Simple Machines the same year as Nopalitos.

eras.title: Last call at the goodbye party
eras.text: Simple Machines wound down in 1998, and the band's last show was part of its goodbye party.

years.big: A band that hardly ever played live, playing live once more
years.h: The last show is Simple Machines' goodbye party
years.p: Grenadine's final performance came at the Simple Machines farewell party, where they played both sad and upbeat songs. Wikipedia lists 1998 as the year the band ended.
years.xp: The label's own band page says the trio played the party, mixing melancholy songs with pop numbers. Toomey and Kristin Thomson closed the label that year.
